

**BiodivPipeline**

**WP2 — BiodivPortal Annotator Module**

Technical Documentation

FU Berlin Software Project SS26  |  June 2026

Project Partners:  Botanischer Garten und Botanisches Museum Berlin (BGBM)

Institut für Angewandte Informatik (InfAI)  |  Supervisor: Prof. Dr. Adrian Paschke

# **1\. Overview**

WP2 is the semantic annotation module of the BiodivPipeline. Its purpose is to transform raw, free-text biodiversity collection records into FAIR-compliant linked data by resolving species names, localities, habitats, and other domain terms against curated ontologies from the BiodivPortal.

The module is built around the GFBio BiodivPortal Annotator REST API and is integrated into the nf-core pipeline as an independent, reusable Nextflow module. It works in combination with the WP2 Recommender sub-module, which determines the best ontology per data field before annotation begins.

The annotation workflow produces three primary output files:

* **annotated.jsonld** – a JSON-LD file containing all resolved ontology URIs and matched concepts per record

* **unresolved\_terms.csv** – a structured report of terms the annotator could not resolve, intended as input for WP5 (Provisional Concept Registration)

* **enriched.csv** – the original input dataset with additional \_URI columns inserted next to each annotated field, as requested by the customer

# **2\. Architecture and Processing Pipeline**

The annotation pipeline follows a six-stage processing model designed for efficiency and correctness on large datasets (validated up to 100,000 records):

| Stage | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| 1\. Field Extraction | Selected semantic fields are extracted from each input record. Technical fields (image URLs, barcodes, identifiers) are excluded from annotation. |
| 2\. Term Normalization | Each field value is normalized using Python's unicodedata NFKC normalization, whitespace-collapsed, and stripped. NFKC converts characters to their canonical decomposed form, ensuring consistent API queries regardless of input encoding. |
| 3\. Deduplication | Unique terms are collected across all records using a field::term key. Each unique term is annotated only once, with results reused across all records containing that term. This significantly reduces API call volume on large datasets. |
| 4\. Parallel Annotation | Unique terms are annotated in parallel using a ThreadPoolExecutor (max\_workers=10). Each term is sent to the BiodivPortal Annotator with a per-field ontology filter derived from the recommender output (ontology\_config.json). |
| 5\. Result Assembly | Annotation results are mapped back to each record. Duplicate annotations (same concept appearing from multiple fields) are removed using a (matched\_text, class\_id, ontology) key. |
| 6\. Output Generation | Three output files are written: annotated.jsonld, unresolved\_terms.csv, and enriched.csv. |

## **2.1 Annotated Fields**

The following fields from the BGBM dataset (Belege\_aus\_D.csv) are selected for semantic annotation. Fields were chosen based on their semantic value for biodiversity data — technical fields such as image links, barcodes, and identifiers are excluded.

| Field | Semantic Category | Recommended Ontology | Confidence Score | Decision |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FullNameCache | Taxon | NCBITAXON | 0.656 | use |
| NameCache | Taxon | NCBITAXON | 0.647 | use |
| Genus | Taxon | NCBITAXON | 0.645 | use |
| Family | Taxon | NCBITAXON | 0.631 | use |
| Locality | Location | ENVO | 0.531 | review |
| Country | Location | LSLIFE | 0.434 | review |
| FundortUNdOeko | Ecology / Habitat | ISOCOUNTRIES | 0.407 | review |
| TitelEtikett | Expedition / Note | — | — | — |
| Expeditionsangabe | Expedition / Note | — | — | — |

*Note: Ontology recommendations and confidence scores are sourced from the recommender output file (ontology\_config.json), generated by the WP2 Recommender sub-module.*

## **2.2 Recommender Integration**

Before annotation runs, the module loads ontology\_config.json from the bin/ directory. This file is generated by the WP2 Recommender sub-module, which queries the BiodivPortal Recommender API to determine the best ontology for each data field based on a sample of the input data.

The recommender assigns one of three decisions per field, sourced directly from the recommender output JSON:

* **use** — high-confidence recommendation; ontology filter is applied to the annotator call

* **review** — moderate confidence; ontology filter is still applied but the recommendation is flagged for manual review

If ontology\_config.json is not present (e.g. during standalone testing), the module falls back gracefully to annotation without ontology filtering, printing a warning to stdout. This ensures the module remains functional even when the recommender output is unavailable.

# **3\. Requirements**

## **3.1 System Requirements**

* Python 3.10 or higher

* Nextflow 23.x or higher (for pipeline execution)

* Valid BiodivPortal API key (BIODIV\_API\_KEY)

## **3.2 Python Dependencies**

Install required packages:

pip install requests python-dotenv

Standard library modules used (no installation required): os, csv, json, time, unicodedata, argparse, concurrent.futures

## **3.3 API Key Setup**

The BiodivPortal API key must be exported as an environment variable before running the module. This is a requirement from the infrastructure team:

export BIODIV\_API\_KEY="your\_key\_here"

In Nextflow execution, the key is passed via the \--biodiv\_api\_key pipeline parameter and exported automatically inside the process script.

# **4\. Usage**

## **4.1 Run Directly with Python**

For local development and testing:

python modules/local/biodiv\_annotate/bin/annotate\_biodiv.py \\

  \--input test\_data/Belege\_aus\_D.csv \\

  \--out-json results/annotation/annotated.jsonld \\

  \--out-unresolved results/annotation/unresolved\_terms.csv \\

  \--out-enriched-csv results/annotation/enriched.csv \\

  \--max-rows 100

## **4.2 Run with Nextflow**

export BIODIV\_API\_KEY="your\_key\_here"

\~/nextflow run modules/local/biodiv\_annotate/main.nf \\

  \--csv test\_data/Belege\_aus\_D.csv \\

  \--biodiv\_api\_key $BIODIV\_API\_KEY \\

  \--max\_rows 1000

## **4.3 CLI Parameters**

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| \--input | data/Belege\_aus\_D.csv | Path to input CSV file |
| \--out-json | results/annotation/annotated.jsonld | Output path for JSON-LD annotations |
| \--out-unresolved | results/annotation/unresolved\_terms.csv | Output path for unresolved terms CSV |
| \--out-enriched-csv | results/annotation/enriched.csv | Output path for URI-enriched CSV |
| \--max-rows | 100000 | Maximum number of rows to process |

# **5\. Output Files**

## **5.1 annotated.jsonld**

A JSON-LD file containing the full annotation results for all processed records. The file uses schema.org terms in the @context to ensure semantic interoperability. Each record in the @graph array contains:

* **record\_id** – the HerbariumID of the source record

* **source\_fields** – the original field values that were annotated

* **annotation\_count** – total number of resolved annotations for this record

* **annotations** – list of resolved concepts, each containing: source\_field, matched\_text, match\_type (PREF/SYN), character positions (from/to), class\_id (ontology URI), ontology name, ontology\_url, ui\_link, and suspicious\_short\_match flag

Real example from BGBM dataset (record B100000328):

{

  "record\_id": "B100000328",

  "source\_fields": {

    "FullNameCache": "Hieracium bauhini var. pilosius Zahn",

    "Genus": "Hieracium",

    "Family": "ASTERACEAE",

    "Country": "Germany"

  },

  "annotation\_count": 3,

  "annotations": \[

    {

      "source\_field": "FullNameCache",

      "matched\_text": "HIERACIUM BAUHINI",

      "match\_type": "SYN",

      "class\_id": "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/NCBITaxon\_221189",

      "ontology": "NCBITAXON",

      "suspicious\_short\_match": false

    },

    {

      "source\_field": "Family",

      "matched\_text": "ASTERACEAE",

      "match\_type": "PREF",

      "class\_id": "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/NCBITaxon\_4210",

      "ontology": "NCBITAXON",

      "suspicious\_short\_match": false

    }

  \]

}

![][image1]

## **5.2 unresolved\_terms.csv**

A CSV file containing terms that could not be resolved by the annotator. This file is designed as direct input for WP5 (Provisional Concept Identification and Registration). Each row represents a unique unresolved term, aggregated across all records that contain it.

| Column | Description | Example |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| source\_field | Field name from which the term was extracted | Locality |
| original\_term | Raw term as it appeared in the input CSV | Koenigsberg i. Franken... |
| normalized\_term | NFKC-normalized, whitespace-collapsed version sent to API | Koenigsberg i. Franken... |
| suggested\_category | Semantic category: taxon, location, ecology\_or\_habitat, expedition\_or\_note | location |
| reason | Why annotation failed: no\_annotation\_returned or api\_error with HTTP status | no\_annotation\_returned |
| ontology\_filter | Ontology filter applied during the failed annotation attempt | ENVO |
| count | Number of records containing this unresolved term | 3 |
| record\_ids | Pipe-separated list of HerbariumIDs where this term appears | B100000328|B100000329 |
| example\_\* | Context columns (FullNameCache, Genus, Family, etc.) from first occurrence for downstream enrichment | Hieracium bauhini... |

*Note: Country (Germany) appears as unresolved in the sample output because the LSLIFE ontology does not contain a matching concept for this term at the whole-word level. This is expected behavior – the term is correctly passed to WP5 for provisional concept registration.*

![][image2]

## **5.3 enriched.csv**

The original input CSV with additional \_URI columns inserted immediately to the right of each annotated field. All original columns are preserved exactly in their original order. URI columns contain the resolved ontology URI from the first matching annotation using the recommended ontology for that field.

Column structure (excerpt from real output):

HerbariumID | Family | Family\_URI | FullNameCache | FullNameCache\_URI | Country | Country\_URI | ...

B100000328 | ASTERACEAE | http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/NCBITaxon\_4210

           | Hieracium bauhini var. pilosius Zahn | http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/NCBITaxon\_221189

           | Germany | (empty — not resolved by LSLIFE)

If no annotation was found for a field, the corresponding \_URI column is left empty. All non-annotated columns pass through unchanged. The file can be directly used as an enriched dataset for downstream pipeline steps and RDF transformation in WP8.

![][image3]

## **5.4 versions.yml**

A Nextflow-standard versions file capturing the runtime tool versions used during execution:

BIODIV\_ANNOTATE:

  annotate\_biodiv: "0.1.0"

  python: "3.12.x"

  requests: "2.x.x"

# **6\. Performance and Scalability**

The module was validated against the real BGBM dataset (Belege\_aus\_D.csv) at multiple scales using both direct Python execution and Nextflow execution:

| Dataset Size | Approx. Unique Terms | Runtime | Execution Method |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 30 rows | \~41 terms | \~3 seconds | Python \+ Nextflow \+ nf-test |
| 300 rows | \~150 terms | \~15 seconds | Python |
| 3,000 rows | \~600 terms | \~2 minutes | Python |
| 5,000 rows | \~900 terms | \~3 minutes | Python |
| 50,000 rows | \~5,000 terms | \~20 minutes | Python |
| 100,000 rows | \~9,000 terms | \~25 minutes | Python (full dataset) |

Performance is primarily determined by the number of unique terms rather than total record count, due to the deduplication strategy. Parallel execution with 10 workers provides a significant throughput improvement over sequential annotation, particularly on datasets with many unique species names.

# **7\. Error Handling and Resilience**

The module is designed to be resilient to partial failures — a single failed annotation does not stop the pipeline run:

| Error Scenario | Handling Strategy | Output Effect |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| API timeout / connection error | Up to 3 retries with exponential backoff (2s, 4s, 8s) | Term added to unresolved\_terms.csv with reason api\_error |
| Invalid JSON response from API | Caught and re-raised as RuntimeError with context | Term added to unresolved\_terms.csv |
| Missing BIODIV\_API\_KEY | Raises ValueError immediately with clear message | Process exits with error — pipeline stops |
| Missing ontology\_config.json | Warning printed to stdout, annotation continues without filter | All terms annotated without ontology restriction |
| Term not found in any ontology | No annotation returned — term classified as unresolved | Term added to unresolved\_terms.csv with no\_annotation\_returned |

# **8\. Testing**

## **8.1 Unit Tests (pytest)**

40 unit tests covering all core functions. Tests run without requiring an API key and use mocked API responses where needed.

Location:

modules/local/biodiv\_annotate/tests/test\_annotate\_biodiv.py

Run with:

pytest modules/local/biodiv\_annotate/tests/test\_annotate\_biodiv.py \-v

| Test Group | Functions Covered | Tests |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| normalize\_term | NFKC normalization, whitespace collapsing, None/empty handling, unicode, special chars | 7 |
| guess\_category | Correct category for all 9 annotated fields, unknown fields, empty string | 6 |
| get\_ontology\_name | URL parsing, trailing slash handling, empty string, None | 4 |
| remove\_duplicates | Exact duplicate removal, different ontologies kept, empty list, order preservation | 5 |
| collect\_terms | Term collection structure, deduplication, occurrence tracking, empty field skipping | 5 |
| simplify\_response | API response parsing, PREF/SYN match types, suspicious short match detection | 4 |
| annotate\_term (mocked) | Success path, API request error, unexpected error, ontology filter passed correctly | 4 |
| save\_enriched\_csv | URI column creation, correct URI values, empty URI for unresolved, original columns preserved | 5 |
| Total |  | 40 |

All 40 tests pass. Example output:

collected 40 items

test\_normalize\_term\_basic PASSED

test\_normalize\_term\_strips\_whitespace PASSED

test\_normalize\_term\_collapses\_spaces PASSED

...

test\_save\_enriched\_csv\_original\_columns\_preserved PASSED

40 passed in 0.18s

![][image4]

## **8.2 Nextflow Module Test (nf-test)**

Module-level integration test that executes the full process against a real test CSV and validates all four outputs.

Location:

modules/local/biodiv\_annotate/tests/main.nf.test

Run with:

nf-test test modules/local/biodiv\_annotate/tests/main.nf.test

Verified assertions:

* Process exits with success status

* annotated.jsonld exists and contains valid @context, @graph, record\_id, annotations keys

* unresolved\_terms.csv exists and contains all required columns (source\_field, original\_term, normalized\_term, suggested\_category, record\_ids)

* enriched.csv exists and contains HerbariumID column and at least one \_URI column

* versions.yml exists and references BIODIV\_ANNOTATE and annotate\_biodiv

## **8.3 Integration Testing**

End-to-end runs were performed on the real BGBM dataset at 30, 300, 3,000, 5,000, 50,000, and 100,000 rows via both direct Python execution and Nextflow execution. All runs completed successfully, producing correct output files.

# **9\. Module Structure**

modules/local/biodiv\_annotate/

├── bin/

│   ├── annotate\_biodiv.py       \# Main annotation script

│   └── ontology\_config.json     \# Recommender output (field to ontology mapping)

├── tests/

│   ├── main.nf.test             \# Nextflow module integration test

│   └── test\_annotate\_biodiv.py  \# pytest unit tests (40 tests)

└── main.nf                      \# Nextflow process definition

# **10\. Downstream Integration**

WP2 outputs are designed for direct consumption by downstream pipeline modules:

| Output File | Consumed by | Purpose |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| annotated.jsonld | WP8 — RDF Matching and Transformation | Provides resolved ontology URIs for RDF triple generation against Darwin Core / ABCD ontologies |
| unresolved\_terms.csv | WP5 — Provisional Concept Registration | Terms absent from existing vocabularies to be registered as provisional concepts in BiodivPortal |
| enriched.csv | WP1 — nf-core Pipeline / WP8 | URI-enriched dataset passed as FAIR-compliant linked data to downstream processing steps |

# **11\. Requirements Compliance (Lastenheft)**

The following table maps all implemented features to the requirements defined in the project Lastenheft for Requirement 2 — BiodivPortal Annotator Integration:

| Requirement | Status | Implementation Detail |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Wrap the BiodivPortal Annotator REST API | Done | ask\_annotator() with full parameter support including ontology filter |
| Handle batch submission of records | Done | collect\_terms() collects unique terms; annotate\_unique\_terms() processes in parallel |
| Parse JSON-LD response | Done | simplify\_response() extracts class\_id, ontology, matched\_text, match\_type, position |
| Emit annotated records in downstream-compatible format | Done | annotated.jsonld with schema.org @context for semantic interoperability |
| Error handling | Done | api\_error and unexpected\_error classification; failed terms go to unresolved output |
| Retry logic | Done | 3 retries with exponential backoff (2s, 4s) in ask\_annotator() |
| Rate-limit compliance | Done | WAIT\_BETWEEN\_REQUESTS configurable (default 0); max\_workers=10 prevents flooding |
| Nextflow module | Done | main.nf with 4 output channels: annotations, unresolved, enriched, versions |
| Integration tests | Done | nf-test module test \+ 40 pytest unit tests, all passing |
| URI-enriched CSV output | Done | enriched.csv with \_URI columns interleaved next to source fields (customer request from Naouel Karam) |
| Recommender integration | Done | ontology\_config.json loaded at startup; per-field ontology filter applied to all API calls |
